validated_work_order.understanding:
#25 bundles four follow-ups the review of #7 found and deliberately did not fix there. I re-checked all four against the current tree; three still hold and one has evaporated.

**Finding 1 — mergeTransactions drops `schedule_occurrence` (still reproduces, and it is the real bug).** Both `db.updateTransaction` payloads in `mergeTransactionsNoTransfer` copy `schedule: keep.schedule || drop.schedule` but say nothing about the stamp. I drove it: posted a recurring schedule occurrence (occurrence 2016-12-02), inserted an identical-amount transaction dated 2016-11-12, merged them. Before the merge `getHasTransactionsQuery` matched 1 row; after, the kept row (the earlier one, which inherits `schedule` from the dropped row) carried `schedule_occurrence: null` and the query matched 0. The occurrence reads as unpaid again — the exact regression #7 was filed to close. The reviewer's claim that this re-opens the exact bug #7 fixed is correct.

**Finding 2 — migration file has no trailing newline (still reproduces).** `tail -c 1` on `packages/loot-core/migrations/1790969762045_add_schedule_occurrence_to_transactions.sql` returns `0x3b` (`;`). Every other migration in that directory ends `0x0a`.

**Finding 3 — transfer mirror legs are never stamped (still reproduces, currently inert).** `addTransfer` builds its mirror-leg object with `schedule: transaction.schedule` and no stamp; `updateTransfer` writes the mirror with the same omission. My probe confirms the mirror comes out `schedule_occurrence: null`. The reviewer is right that this does NOT currently re-open the bug — every consumer of `getHasTransactionsQuery` collapses to a `Set` of schedule ids or a boolean (`schedules/app.ts:655`, `schedules/app.ts:602`, `desktop-client/src/hooks/useSchedules.ts:38`), so an extra matching row cannot change an outcome. It is a latent trap, not a live defect, and the fix is the same one line.

**Finding 4 — snapshot churn — does not hold up, and I am dropping it.** The reviewer's own evidence says the churn is a `@@` context-window artefact, that it was verified against main, and that "no code change is required"; the requested remedy was one sentence in the PR body, and that PR is merged. There is nothing here for an implementation. I have carried its concern forward instead, as an explicit instruction that the new transfer test must not use snapshots (see AC-5), so this diff cannot grow the same confusion.

No decisions were recorded for this issue (plan/brief.md is empty), so nothing here overrides anything.
validated_work_order.root_cause: `schedule` and `schedule_occurrence` were introduced as a pair by #7, but #7 only ever taught the WRITE that creates a stamped row (schedules/app.ts:572). Every pre-existing write that copies an existing transaction's schedule onto another row was left untouched, so the two fields can drift apart: a row can end up schedule-linked with no occurrence identity. `db.updateTransaction` drops `undefined` fields (schema-helpers.ts:136) and keeps `null`, which is why these paths silently leave the stamp at its existing value instead of erroring.
validated_work_order.approach:
One rule, applied at every place that copies a transaction's schedule onto another row: the occurrence stamp travels with the schedule link, or not at all.

I audited every write in the repo that propagates `schedule` from one transaction to another, which is the audit #7's work order skipped (it enumerated only the READ paths). There are exactly four, and all four are in this change:

1. `merge.ts:165` — the split branch of `mergeTransactionsNoTransfer` (`keep` gains the dropped row's subtransactions and is marked `is_parent`).
2. `merge.ts:176` — the normal branch.
3. `transfer.ts:68` — `addTransfer`, constructing the mirror leg.
4. `transfer.ts:131` — `updateTransfer`, updating the mirror leg.

Two other sites carry `schedule` and are deliberately NOT touched. `transfer.ts:78` and `:84` write `matchedSchedule` back onto the SAME transaction whose stamp is already correct — nothing is copied between rows. `forecast-schedules.ts:273` copies `schedule` onto a simulated transfer leg, but that leg is never persisted (it exists only in the forecast's in-memory `simulatedTransactions`) and its `sourceTransaction` is built six lines earlier at `:218` with no stamp to copy. `find-schedules.ts:29`'s `schedule: null` is a query filter, not a write.

On the merge expression I specify `??` rather than the `||` used on the line above. A stamp is either a positive `YYYYMMDD` integer or null, so the two operators agree on every reachable value; `??` states "take the dropped row's only when the kept row has none" without implying that `0` is a meaningful date. It is a deliberate difference from the surrounding line and the reviewer should see it as one.

On `updateTransfer` I specify `transaction.schedule_occurrence` verbatim rather than `?? null`, and this is load-bearing. `conform()` drops `undefined` from an update (schema-helpers.ts:136) but writes `null`, so a partial update that omits the field leaves the mirror alone — exactly how the `schedule` line above it already behaves — while an explicit `null` from the client clears the stamp alongside the schedule link. `?? null` would silently wipe the mirror's stamp on every partial API update that never mentioned it.

The migration fix is a one-byte append. Migrations are keyed by filename, not content, so an already-migrated database is unaffected.

No release note: the behaviour this corrects was introduced by #7, whose note (`upcoming-release-notes/keep-posted-schedules-paid-today.md`) is still unreleased. Fixing it before it ships needs no second note.

files.change:
In BOTH `db.updateTransaction` payloads inside `mergeTransactionsNoTransfer` — the split branch (line 165, `... as unknown as TransactionEntity`) and the normal branch (line 176, `... as TransactionEntity`) — add one line immediately after the existing `schedule: keep.schedule || drop.schedule,`:

      schedule_occurrence: keep.schedule_occurrence ?? drop.schedule_occurrence,

Both branches are named by the review (lines 165 and 176) and both need it; a fix to only the normal branch leaves the split path broken. `??` is deliberate — see approach. Keep the existing casts unchanged; `TransactionEntity.schedule_occurrence` is `string | null | undefined` so the value type-checks against the optional field with no cast change.

files.change:

1. In the `transferTransaction` object literal in `addTransfer` (line 68), add `schedule_occurrence: transaction.schedule_occurrence,` so the auto-created mirror leg inherits the main leg's occurrence identity. It reaches the insert via the existing `db.insertTransaction({ ...transferTransaction, notes, cleared, schedule: matchedSchedule })` spread — do not add it to that call site separately.
2. In the `db.updateTransaction` payload in `updateTransfer` (line 131), add `schedule_occurrence: transaction.schedule_occurrence,`.

Pass the value through verbatim in both places. Do NOT write `?? null`: `conform()` drops `undefined` from an update but writes `null`, so a partial update that omits the field must leave the mirror alone — which is precisely how the `schedule` line above behaves. `?? null` would wipe the mirror's stamp on any partial API update that never mentioned it.

cases: carries the occurrence stamp from the dropped transaction when the kept transaction has none — mirrors the existing 'preserves schedule link from dropped transaction when kept transaction has none' case: t1 banksynced and unstamped (the keep), t2 stamped with a schedule and a schedule_occurrence (the drop); after the merge the single surviving row has both `schedule` and `schedule_occurrence` equal to t2's

preserves the kept transaction's stamp when the dropped row has none — guards against the new line clobbering an existing stamp with `undefined`

carries the occurrence stamp in the split branch — the branch at merge.ts:165 is a different `db.updateTransaction` call and needs its own case: keep is a plain banksynced transaction, drop is a stamped split parent with children; after the merge the kept row must have gained `schedule`, `schedule_occurrence` and `is_parent`

the mirror leg carries the schedule and occurrence stamp of its main leg — insert a transaction with a schedule, a schedule_occurrence and a transfer payee, call `transfer.onInsert`, then read both rows with a plain `db.all` and assert the mirror has the same `schedule` AND the same `schedule_occurrence` as the main leg
the stamp survives an update of the main leg — change the main leg's date, call `transfer.onUpdate`, and assert the mirror still carries both fields

clearing the schedule link on the main leg clears the stamp on the mirror too — assert a main leg sent with `schedule: null, schedule_occurrence: null` leaves the mirror with both null, which is the case the `??` in updateTransfer is there to handle

merging a posted occurrence into an earlier duplicate does not un-pay the schedule — inside the existing `describe('occurrence stamp')` block, which already has `createRecurringSchedule`, `postTransaction`, `readMatches` and the NEXT_DATE fixture: post an occurrence, insert an identical-amount transaction dated earlier, call `mergeTransactions([{ id: postedId }, { id: duplicateId }])`, then assert (a) the id that `mergeTransactions` returns has `schedule_occurrence` equal to NEXT_DATE, and (b) `readMatches(scheduleId)` returns exactly one row. Before this fix (b) is 0. Note that the dropped row is tombstoned rather than physically deleted, so `readMatches` sees one live row — do not assert on raw `SELECT * FROM transactions` counts, which include tombstones

qa_script: Bring the app up (`yarn start`, or `yarn start:server-dev`), open a budget with 'View demo' so there is real data to merge against.

Schedules page: create a recurring schedule — a name, a fixed amount (e.g. 100 out), a monthly date condition on a specific day. Post its current occurrence with the schedule's post/Pay action. Confirm the schedule now reads as paid for that occurrence.
In that account's register, manually add a second transaction with the SAME amount dated roughly three weeks EARLIER than the posted one. It must be the identical amount — merge refuses a mismatch.
Select exactly those two rows and use Merge. Confirm one row survives and still carries the schedule link.
Reload and return to the Schedules page. The occurrence must still read as paid. Before this fix it flips back to 'Due' and the upcoming row comes back — that flip is the bug.

Transfer leg (expected to be a no-op on screen, confirm it stays one): take a schedule-posted transaction and change its payee to another account's transfer payee. A mirror row appears in the other account. Nothing may duplicate, disappear, or change the schedule's paid status.
Repeat step 6 by editing the main leg's date afterwards. The mirror must still track it and the schedule must still read as paid.
No new console errors, no new rows in either account's register beyond the expected mirror, and `yarn workspace @actual-app/core run test:node` green.
risks: The merge change means a kept row can acquire a stamp it did not have, sourced from the dropped row. The invariant that makes this safe is that stamp and schedule link are written by the SAME expression, so they can never disagree: `schedule: keep.schedule || drop.schedule` picks keep's schedule whenever keep has one, and in that case keep necessarily has a meaningful stamp or none at all. If a future edit ever decouples those two lines the invariant breaks, so keep them adjacent.

The transfer change means two rows can now match the same occurrence. Every consumer of `getHasTransactionsQuery` collapses to a `Set` of schedule ids or a boolean — `schedules/app.ts:655` (advanceSchedulesService), `schedules/app.ts:602` (hasTransactionForSchedule), `desktop-client/src/hooks/useSchedules.ts:38` (loadStatuses) — so an additional matching row cannot change any of their outcomes. Verified by reading all three; none counts rows.

`forecast-schedules.ts:273` propagates `schedule` to a simulated transfer leg without a stamp and is deliberately left alone. It is not a write path — the row is never persisted — but a future change that persists forecast rows would have to revisit it.

No new hosts, no network calls, no new dependencies. Nothing in this change touches a `forbidden_paths` entry: `packages/loot-core/migrations/**` is not among them (only `packages/ci-actions/src/migrations/**`, `packages/loot-core/src/mocks/migrations/**` and `packages/loot-core/src/server/migrate/**` are), so the migration edit is permitted.
out_of_scope: Review finding 4 (the ~44 lines of unexplained churn in transfer.test.ts.snap): dropped. The reviewer's own evidence establishes it as a `@@` context-window artefact that reproduces on unmodified main, states 'no code change is required', and asks only for a sentence in the PR body — a PR that is now merged. There is nothing here to implement. The concern is honoured instead by AC-5 and by requiring the new transfer test not to use snapshots.

forecast-schedules.ts:273: the simulated transfer leg copies `schedule` from a `sourceTransaction` built at :218 with no stamp, and is never persisted — there is no stamp to copy and no row to write. Changing it would ship on its own and fixes nothing observable.

Whether a schedule-posted transaction's stamp should be cleared when a user removes the schedule link by any means other than the transfer paths above. That is a separate audit of the rule engine and the schedules UI; this ticket fixes the four write paths the review named and that I audited.

A release note. The behaviour being corrected shipped unreleased with #7 — `upcoming-release-notes/keep-posted-schedules-paid-today.md` is still pending — so there is nothing for a second note to tell a user about.

alternatives_considered.approach: Clear the stamp whenever the schedule link is cleared (a shared helper or an invariant enforced in db/aql), rather than copying the stamp at each of the four write paths.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It does not fix finding 1 at all. The merge bug is not a missing clear, it is a missing copy: keep.schedule and drop.schedule are different values and the code already merges them by hand. A guard that only enforces 'no stamp without a schedule' would have prevented neither the merge nor the transfer mirror leg.

alternatives_considered.approach: Stop propagating `schedule` to the transfer mirror leg altogether, so a mirror row is never schedule-linked.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A behaviour change well beyond what the review asked for, in a path (#7) that is already out and would alter the mirror's schedule-driven rule resolution and the Schedules page. The reviewer explicitly asked for the stamp to be carried, and measured the current behaviour as inert.

alternatives_considered.approach: Drop finding 1 as 'pre-existing, inherited rather than introduced' and file it separately.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The review's own reasoning rejects this: the stamp design is unreleased, the defect exists only because of the new column, and it defeats the central guarantee of the change it belongs to. Splitting it would ship the feature with a known hole in it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Write `schedule_occurrence: keep.schedule_occurrence || drop.schedule_occurrence`, matching the `||` on the line above.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Equivalent on every reachable value (a stamp is a positive YYYYMMDD integer or null, so `0` and `''` cannot occur), but `??` states the intent precisely. Kept `??` and flagged the deliberate difference from the surrounding line so a reviewer reads it as a choice.

assumptions: `schedule_occurrence` can only ever be null or a positive YYYYMMDD integer (the migration declares it INTEGER and #7 writes `schedule.next_date` through it), so `??` and `||` behave identically here and no falsy-but-valid stamp exists.

The desktop client sends a whole transaction entity on edit, so `transaction.schedule_occurrence` is present when the UI updates a schedule-posted transaction. This is why `updateTransfer` can pass the value through verbatim; a caller that sends only `{ id, notes }` leaves the mirror's stamp alone, which is the intended and safe direction.

`db.getTransaction` returns rows read back through the AQL schema, so `keep.schedule_occurrence` / `drop.schedule_occurrence` are `null` rather than `undefined` for an unstamped row — either way `??` treats them the same.

Merges of two transactions that are each stamped for DIFFERENT schedules already pick one schedule (`keep.schedule || drop.schedule`); this change makes the stamp follow that same pick, rather than introducing a new selection rule.
unknowns: I could not exercise the browser path in qa_script — this checkout has no running app and QA drives that. Steps 2-5 are written from the code (schedules/app.ts handlers, useSchedules' loadStatuses, SelectedTransactionsButton.tsx's 'merge-transactions' action), not from a live session.

Whether any real rule in a user's rule set can assign a different schedule to a transfer mirror leg via `runRules`. If it can, the mirror would carry a stamp belonging to the main leg's schedule. I judged this too speculative to guard against in this diff — it is already true of the `schedule` field on the same line — and recorded it as a residual risk rather than adding a condition the review did not ask for.
residual_risks: In `addTransfer`, `runRules` may assign a different schedule to the mirror leg than the main leg's (`matchedSchedule = schedule ?? transaction.schedule`). The stamp is copied unconditionally alongside it, so in that (unverified) case the mirror would carry a schedule and a stamp that belong to different schedules. This is pre-existing behaviour of the `schedule` field on the same object, not something this change introduces; the guard, if one is ever wanted, belongs on both fields together.
